Question Text: Two compact objects of masses 3 kg and 7 kg are dropped together in a vacuum from the same height. Predict their accelerations and explain why one does not “fall faster” simply because it is heavier.
Answer 1: Both accelerate downward at the same gravitational acceleration, about 10 m/s², when air resistance is ignored.
Answer 2: The heavier object has five times the acceleration.
Answer 4: Both have zero acceleration once released.

Question Text: An object starts from rest and falls freely for 1 s. Using g ≈ 10 m/s², determine the speed gained.
Answer 1: about 10 m/s downward
Answer 2: about 1 m/s downward
Answer 4: about 10 m/s upward

Question Text: Use the ideal free-fall table to compare how distance fallen changes from one second to the next. Then explain why a sheet of paper falling through air may not follow this pattern.
Answer 1: Distance increases by progressively larger amounts because speed is increasing; a sheet of paper can deviate because air resistance is significant.
Answer 2: Equal distances are covered each second, and air has no effect.
Answer 3: Distance decreases each second because gravity weakens.
Answer 4: Any falling object must exactly match the table.
